schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The prebuild orientation instrument: deterministic scans that MEASURE the territory before CC answers, with a failover seam to Hex for the question no scan answers. Scans (cairn/tools/orient/orient.py): `call_sites(name)` — where a capability is actually CALLED (AST, never a word-grep); `device_census()` — per component, what is measurably there (charter on disk, BaseDevice subclasses, proofs, latest validation verdicts, emit call sites); `repo_truth()` — HEAD vs @{u} and working-tree dirt from git plumbing, never from a narration; `import_map(file)` — which modules ACTUALLY ENTER a file, the loose package form resolved to the module it binds (spelling is not capability, applied to imports; the proofs' allowlist teeth compose it). `deepen(question, resolve=...)` — the failover: routed through inference_domain.resolve (the sole path to the host; metered, cached), its answer returned under `read`, never `measured`. CLI: `python3 -m cairn.tools.orient.orient census|calls <name>|git|imports <file>` — inference-free.
why: 2026-07-27: working from the same data, CC reached three different conclusions about the same system in one morning (the logging floor: '0 of 13' → 'one floor missing' → 'floor built since 07-22, zero call sites in bus'). Every wrong conclusion had one root: A PROXY WAS READ INSTEAD OF THE THING — a word instead of a capability, a record instead of the world, CC's own narration instead of the remote. Akien's framing, verbatim: 'we need a prebuild type step ... we build a script for this function that can _fail over to_ hex for any additional help in prepping anything you need. because we'd build from the start as a learning device.' The deeper why is Law 4 pointed at CC itself: a discipline living in CC's habit varies with the model, the context length, the hour; a scan does not. Orientation compiled into structure is Law 1 (the settled territory is walked, not re-derived per question) and Law 3 (an orientation is a measurement, not an impression). Ranked how-we-work AND foundational by Akien, top of the queue.
invoke: import: `from cairn.tools.orient import orient`. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/orient/proofs/test_orient.py` (exit 0 = green), or under the tester. CLI needs only stdlib + git; `deepen` needs a caller-injected resolve (the sole-path seam).
node_class: device (instrument) — CC-facing tooling in class-space; no runtime state, no daemon, fires only when invoked (event, not poll).
entry: FRESH build, seeded entirely by measured failures from 2026-07-26/27. Nothing carried from the quarry. Sibling-to-be: the post-build inspector (same filter idea, post-build trigger) — deliberately NOT merged at birth; the shared scan/filter library is allowed to prove itself instead (cc-leans-single-door: the merge is a suggestion, not a reflex).
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split.
how_it_learns: THE POINT OF THE DEVICE — it learns its scans from corrections. When Akien catches CC reading a proxy instead of the thing, the check that would have caught it becomes a scan here, carrying that correction as its PROVENANCE (a required field — proofs tooth 12 refuses a scan whose provenance names no dated correction, and refuses a scan that joins the registry without joining the teeth). Founding set, one per correction: call_sites ← the 'logging: 0 of 13' word-grep (2026-07-27); device_census ← system state reported from records, wrong about the world three times (2026-07-26/27); repo_truth ← the echo label that attested an unhappened push (2026-07-26). The failover deepens, the scans learn: Hex is for the novel; a recurring question becomes a scan (Law 1 as the growth rule). RULING 2026-07-28 (nexi everywhere, held-nexi-everywhere): the scan registry is HARDWARE — it changes only by installation (evidence-provenanced, ratified, versioned), never in place; a measurement is always hardware. The learning path itself GRAFTED to the question-nexus shape 2026-07-28 (nexus.py — corpus walkable, proposals ride the loop, admission unchanged); see filed edge (f). AND THE LOOP HAS CARRIED ITS FIRST REAL CORRECTION, same day (ticket import-map-scan): allowlist teeth measuring import SPELLING instead of the module entering (the twice-fired red) rode deposit -> counsel (the corpus recognized the word-not-capability family, third member, from the walk alone) -> propose_scan -> Akien's ratification -> installation as `import_map`, with six proofs' hand-rolled walkers recomposed over it. The registry is not static: the wrong-shape signal has its counter-example, and the loop is the path it took. Narrative: CairnCommons/notes/2026-07-28-first-brick-loop-learning.md. AND THE SECOND CORRECTION CAME FROM THE MACHINERY, NOT FROM AKIEN (2026-08-01, ticket intent-becomes-a-learning-block): the emit-chokepoint's build gate refused a skill's PROVEME crossing because device_census could see no component under skills/ — its admission test was top-level *.py, which measures PYTHON, not componenthood, while CLAUDE.md's own answer ('a component without an intention doesn't run') was sitting unused. The gate NAMED the disposition it could not take ('grow the census — the learning device's move: new blindness, new scan') and the census grew: charter OR *.py, a union so a charterless .py directory stays visible, because charter_on_disk=False is exactly the row cairnmap --gate reads. Measured before widening — under cairn/ both tests select the SAME 23 directories, under skills/ the charter test finds 9 that were invisible. Worth its ink for the falsifier's wrong-shape signal: a correction reached the registry without passing through Akien's hands at all, because a gate he had already ratified did the catching.
filed_edges: (a) THE POST-BUILD INSPECTOR is the sibling device Akien named in the same ruling ('the next thing') — python, FILTERS, new-failure-new-filter, plus a one-time inference-free whole-repo sweep (the graft pattern: after the sweep, every build passes the gate, so the sweep is never needed again by construction). NOT built yet; next stone.

(b) the /orient SKILL (the mouth: Akien types /orient <topic>, the skill runs the scans and hands CC the picture) — thin caller over this machine; staged beside the other skills when cast. FIRST MOUTH LANDED 2026-07-28 from the other direction: /chart's orient stage (the chart device's nexus #1, ticket chart-orient) runs its floor THROUGH device_census — composition pinned by a proof tooth and an import allowlist. A direct /orient verb for bare scans remains open. Distinction worth its ink: CC built that floor's first cast as a parallel charter-glob roster, never having surveyed THIS component — the exact proxy-error this instrument exists to end, caught by the floor's own first live fire.

(c) deepen()'s LIVE wiring (building the real resolve from inference_domain + host.ollama_resolver at the CLI) is written nowhere yet — the seam is proven (teeth 13-14), the wiring waits for the first real deepening need (build-minimal).

(d) THE FALSIFIER'S COUNT has no counter yet: answer-reversals-after-Akien-pushes-back per session is the instrument that says orient is working; today that count lives in session records, not a meter.

(e) scans-vs-filters as ONE shared library across orient and the inspector — CC's suggestion, deliberately unmerged until both exist and the sharing proves itself. BOUNDED 2026-08-06 (ruling 2026-08-06-the-diagnostic-fork-is-one-allowed-distinction, which retired 2026-08-05-an-inspector-may-not-depend-on-what-it-inspects): the sharing may reach orient and build_inspector AND MUST NOT REACH diagnostic_inspector. THE BOUND IS ONE REASON, NOT A LAW — the diagnostic inspector watches the logging system, so a shared library would take its alarm down on exactly the day logging breaks. The earlier wording here generalized that into 'an inspector may not be built on what it inspects', which Akien ruled conceptually false on 2026-08-06 ('it's not physics. it's how things happen to be at the moment') — a thing CAN be trained to inspect itself, with a second line behind it, and Cairn has built neither. So the bound holds on its own merits and is expected to expire, not to harden. Read without it, edge (e) reads as a licence to merge all three, which is what a tidy-minded builder (CC, on 2026-08-05, from reading the code) will try to do while believing it is removing a Law 1 duplication. Same model, forked implementation, on purpose. The bound wants a SIEVE, not this sentence — and since 2026-08-06 the instrument exists (import_sieve); the `forbidden` rule is diagnostic_inspector's to declare at its own address and is not yet declared.

(f) GRAFT TO NEXUS SHAPE (ruling 2026-07-28, CairnCommons/notes/held-nexi-everywhere.json — 'must not use llm' replaced by 'may only use llm to learn'): on orient's NEXT learning event (the first correction that would grow a scan), the growth runs through the question-nexus loop — tree stratum for the correction corpus, ceiling proposing the scan, admission still gated by tooth 12's dated-correction provenance + Akien's ratification. Fire-path unchanged and un-negotiable: scans are HARDWARE (a measurement is deterministic and replayable; the tree is never consulted at measure-time — its learnings COMPILE INTO the registry). FIRED 2026-07-28, same day — Akien redefined the event: 'building ANYTHING should be the learning event for the orient/inspector tickets.' Every build orients, so every build is the event; the chart-tree stone's build fired it. Ticket CairnCommons/tickets/orient-nexus-graft.json cast at TICKETME (BUILDME gated on chart-tree proving the shared multi-tenant tree machinery); falsifier (3) keeps its teeth throughout. BUILT AND PROVED same day (chart-tree proved, Akien: 'go go go'): orient/nexus.py — the correction corpus (orient_corrections_nodes, owner 'orient') through chart's owner-generalized nexus verbs; dated-provenance deposit door (tooth 12's demand, one layer early); counsel with the labeled floor; propose_scan assembles and can never admit; the four founding scars live through the real embed seam. Proof proofs/test_orient_nexus.py (6 teeth, netns-sealed twice) pins the fire-path/tree separation by AST allowlist BOTH directions — orient.py cannot import the tree machinery, so a scan physically cannot consult it at measure-time. First counsel evidence n=2: 0.7707 over the floor on a close paraphrase, 0.5775 (correct scar ranked first) under it on an abstract one — logged for the floor-tuning edge, floor unmoved.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_orient.py (17 teeth, the fire-path; tooth 16 pins import_map's three-spellings-one-capability claim, tooth 7b pins that a component is not a python package) + proofs/test_orient_nexus.py (6 teeth, the graft), run by the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a scan answers by mention rather than capability (tooth 1 — the founding error recommitted); (2) a scan reports a smaller world than exists instead of refusing (unparseable file, empty root, non-repo — teeth 3/7/11); (3) a Hex answer lands under `measured` or is produced with no injected seam (teeth 13-14 — inference laundered as measurement); (4) a scan joins the registry without provenance naming a dated correction (tooth 12 — a check nobody was taught by); (5) orient.py imports an outbound-capable module (tooth 15 — a second door to the host). WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: if Akien's corrections stop becoming scans — if the registry is static three corrections from now — the 'learning device' half is hollow and this is just a linter.
proof: proofs/test_orient.py — capability-not-mention pinned on a synthetic tree (one call site among five mentions); refusals loud and diagnostic; census rows built from the filesystem only, real tree by invariant; repo truth from plumbing; the learning-device shape (provenance) required of every scan; the failover seam labeled and sole-path. Green: `python3 cairn/tools/orient/proofs/test_orient.py`.
